title: Shipped TweetNaCl deterministic primitive vectors and bounded tamper cases
oracle: Actual shipped tweetnacl→tweetnacl-1.0.3 pure JavaScript cryptographic operations in the worker realm. Literal NIST SHA512, RFC7748 X25519, RFC8032 Ed25519 and pinned upstream libsodium NaCl box/secretbox vectors supply independent expected bytes. Generated SHA512 expectations use node:crypto createHash in the test host outside the worker; only expected typed JSON bytes enter the realm. Byte-tamper and wrong-size cases characterize selected verification/authentication rejection and argument guards. No host crypto provider/functions or custom crypto implementation is injected.

validMessageMatrix.sourceBoundary: Original signing hashes expanded-secret suffix32||message and R32||publicKey32||message; selected message lengths straddle source-derived prefix-adjusted SHA-512 padding and block boundaries. The source fromSeed expansion always hashes 32 seed bytes independently of message length.
validMessageMatrix.oracle: Actual signatures are compared with independent standard host Ed25519 signatures. Signed-message expectations concatenate the host signature and literal message; verify/open inputs use those independently generated bytes, not an archived sign/open round-trip oracle.

visibleViews.scope: Nonempty sentinel-backed visible views cover message/secret-key/signature/public-key/signed-message inputs; fromSeed visible views use the fixed RFC8032 seed and literal publicKey/seed||publicKey expectations. No backing mutation-isolation or key-identity claim.

signatureExtension.hostOracle: Host node:crypto standard Ed25519 uses the published RFC8032 seed and public key supplied together as OKP JWK d/x. The published public x is supplied, not independently derived from a seed-only host import. Host public-component agreement, two exact empty-message RFC signatures and native verification are checked before generated expectations; generated signatures are 64 bytes and host-verified. KeyObjects, native functions and crypto providers remain outside the worker; only frozen synthetic byte JSON enters it.
signatureExtension.scope: Selected valid signatures/messages and visible inputs only. Existing whole-source pins and default 2000000-work AST exhaustion at1999990 remain unchanged; no zero-gate, full configuration, original provider, PRNG, protocol or security acceptance.

libsodium.adaptation: C low-level vectors prepend 32 zero message bytes; high-level message excludes them. Expected .exp output already prints ciphertext indices 16..162; first 147 bytes are highlevel tag+ciphertext, second copy is the in-place C run. box.c uses RFC7748 Alice secret/Bob public; box.exp matches secretbox.exp. box.before expected key matches independently published secretbox key; no libsodium execution claimed.

exclusions: Only direct shipped bundled pure-JavaScript primitives execute; no cr8712 alias binding, WACryptoDependencies/self.crypto, WhatsApp crypto provider, WACryptoPrimitives, Signal/Noise/ratchet or protocol acceptance.

Original bundle/browser/bootstrap integration, entropy/PRNG/randomBytes/random key generation and no-PRNG exceptions are unexercised. No self/global alias, stub, callback, host crypto provider or guard weakening is supplied.

Full source pins include both modules; incomplete AST budget is preserved at default2m. Zero inventoried gates is not a complete gate inventory, empty finite assignment proof or total configuration cardinality.

Fixed published keys/nonces are test inputs only. Bounded tamper/size vectors do not prove constant-time behavior, full canonical point/signature handling, cryptographic security or all malformed inputs.

Pinned libsodium source supplies vector data only, not execution of libsodium or another named-library adapter. Container execution, production TypeScript suite scheduling, accounts/network and registered-library compliance remain unproven.
